prompt: write a paragraph on why people procrastinate for my psych class, college level
reply: Procrastination is less a failure of time management than a problem of emotion regulation. When a task provokes discomfort — boredom, anxiety, self-doubt, or fear of judgment — delaying it offers immediate relief, and that relief negatively reinforces the avoidance. Temporal discounting compounds the effect: people tend to weigh present costs heavily while discounting future rewards, so the unpleasantness of starting a paper today looms larger than the benefit of a finished draft next week. Perfectionism and low self-efficacy also play a role, since people who doubt their ability to succeed may avoid starting in order to protect their self-image. Understood this way, procrastination is a short-term mood-repair strategy with long-term costs, which helps explain why simply telling someone to "manage their time better" rarely works.

reply: For many teenagers, social media is a genuine source of connection and growth.
